explanations.explanation: All things, baker. John 1:3 says "Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made." That's the whole list, with no leftovers. Even my cookie planet and every oven on it came through Him.

The heavens are in there, but the verse doesn't stop at them. John 1:3 says "Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made." That's a lot bigger than the sky. It's like saying you only made the top layer of the batch when you made the whole thing.

Living creatures are in there, friend, but the verse doesn't draw that fence. John 1:3 says "Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made." Creatures, mountains, oceans, all of it. The word "only" just doesn't show up.

True, baker. John 1:5 says "The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it." The darkness has not overcome the Light. I know a thing or two about dark places, and I'm telling you, it doesn't get the last word.

Not quite, friend. John 1:5 says "The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it." So the darkness has not overcome the Light. The Light is still shining, and the darkness is the one that came up short.

explanations.answer: So everyone might believe through him
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. John 1:7 says he came "…so that through him everyone might believe." He was a witness, and a witness points at someone else. He's like the friend who says "you've GOT to meet my neighbor," and then steps back.

explanations.answer: So people would come to follow him
explanations.explanation: I can see why you'd go there, friend, but the text doesn't say that. John 1:7 says he came to testify about the Light "…so that through him everyone might believe." His job was pointing to the Light. A witness doesn't hand out tickets to his own show.

explanations.answer: So the temple leaders would listen
explanations.explanation: Good guess, but the verse doesn't mention temple leaders at all. John 1:7 says he came as a witness "…so that through him everyone might believe." The word is everyone, friend, not one special group. Keep that word in your pocket.

Not quite, baker. John 1:8 says "He himself was not the Light, but he came to testify about the Light." John was the witness, and the Light was Someone else. A spoon can point at the batch all day, but it's still not the batch.

False is right, friend. John 1:8 says "He himself was not the Light, but he came to testify about the Light." John is the witness, and the Light is Someone else. I think pointing away from yourself like that is pretty humble.
Right, baker. John 1:10 says "…the world did not recognize Him." And that's though the world was made through Him. Picture an old friend looking right at you and having no idea who you are. Ouch.

explanations.answer: It tries to chase Him away
explanations.explanation: That's not what this verse says, friend. John 1:10 says "…the world did not recognize Him." It doesn't say anything about chasing. The world just didn't know who it was looking at.

explanations.answer: It runs and hides from Him
explanations.explanation: Hiding isn't in this verse, baker. John 1:10 says "…the world did not recognize Him." It says that even though the world was made through Him. The word is recognize. The verse doesn't say anything about running.

Children, baker! John 1:12 says He gave them "…the right to become children of God…" That's the word right there. I once lived in a drawer with a twist tie, so a family like that hits me right in the mustache.
Servants is a good guess, friend, but that's not the word here. John 1:12 says He gave them "…the right to become children of God…" Children. That's a seat at the family table.
Good guess, baker, but messengers isn't the word here. John 1:12 says He gave them "…the right to become children of God…" The word is children. Hold onto that one.

Not this time, baker. John 1:13 says these children were "…born not of blood, nor of the desire or will of man, but born of God." So it's not by the will of man. It's God's doing from start to finish.
False is right, friend. John 1:13 says they are "…born not of blood, nor of the desire or will of man, but born of God." So they are not born of the will of man. They are born of God.

explanations.answer: The one and only Son from the Father
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. John 1:14 says "We have seen His glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father…" The writer says "We have seen…" so this is glory that was seen. And the glory belongs to the Son.

explanations.answer: The great prophet sent from the Father
explanations.explanation: Close, friend, but that's not the wording. John 1:14 says "…the glory of the one and only Son from the Father…" The word is Son, not prophet. Keep your eye on that word and you're set.

explanations.answer: The mighty angel sent from the Father
explanations.explanation: An angel did show up in my drawer once, baker, and I can tell you the verse isn't about one. John 1:14 says "…the glory of the one and only Son from the Father…" The Word is the Son. Angels are wonderful, but this is a different thing entirely.

True, baker. In John 1:15 John cried out, "This is He of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me.’…" That sounds like a riddle, but John cries it out loud and clear. Read it twice if it tangles you up, because I had to.

Not false, friend. John 1:15 has John crying out, "He who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me." So he really does say it. Read it again slowly if it makes your head spin. Mine did the first time.

Jesus Christ, baker! John 1:17 says "grace and truth came through Jesus Christ." The law came through Moses, and grace and truth came through Him. Good thing too, because my edges needed a lot of grace.

David is a big name, friend, but he isn't the one here. John 1:17 says "grace and truth came through Jesus Christ." The verse sets Moses on one side and Jesus Christ on the other. David isn't mentioned in it.
Elijah is a good name to know, baker, but not the answer here. John 1:17 says "grace and truth came through Jesus Christ." The verse puts Moses next to Jesus Christ. Elijah isn't mentioned in it.

He has made God known, baker. John 1:18 says "No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father’s side, has made Him known." That's how we get to know what God is like. Through the Son, plain and simple.

That's a good thought, friend, but it's not what the verse says. John 1:18 says the one and only Son "…has made Him known." Remember, the law was given through Moses (John 1:17). The Son's part here is making God known.

explanations.answer: He has built God a temple
explanations.explanation: Building a temple is a big job, baker, but it isn't in this verse. John 1:18 says the one and only Son "…has made Him known." No hammers, no blueprints. He has made God known.
